newsitem.title: USA: Marvel bondholders buy Marvel bank debt.
newsitem.headline: Marvel bondholders buy Marvel bank debt.

text.p: Members of the bondholders committee of Marvel Entertainment Group purchased an undisclosed amount of the company's bank debt and are seeking to buy more, according to a statement filed by the group with the Securities and Exchange Commission.
A spokesman for the bondholders committee, which is led by Carl Icahn, declined any comment.

Sources familiar with the situation said the purchases may signify that Marvel bondholders are interested in obtaining a seat at the table in any negotiations between holders of approximately $725 million in bank debt and the struggling comic book publisher.

In the filing, members of the bondholders group also disclosed that they recently installed a new board of directors at Marvel Holdings Corp, a holding company that owns a 50.03 percent stake in Marvel common stock.
The new board of directors consists of Carl Icahn, Robert Mitchell, treasurer of ACF Industries Inc and Vincent Intrieri, a portfolio manager at Westgate International.
Bondholders are appealing a court ruling preventing them from voting their share of Marvel common stock to oust Marvel's current board of directors.
Oral argument on the appeal is scheduled for May 1, according to the filing.
